subject: Television & Streaming
title: The Kennedy-Nixon Debate Changed Elections
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Kennedy-Nixon Debate Changed Elections usable.

hook.text: In 1960, Kennedy and Nixon debated on live television. Radio listeners thought Nixon won. TV viewers chose Kennedy.

buildup.text: Nixon looked pale, sweaty, and uncomfortable on camera. Kennedy appeared calm, tanned, and confident.

discovery.text: The debate proved that on television, appearance matters as much as substance. Image became inseparable from message.

twist.text: Every presidential candidate since has hired media coaches.

climax.text: Television didn't just cover politics—it transformed politics into a visual medium where presence trumps policy.

punchline.text: A sweaty lip changed how we pick leaders.

quiz.question: What did the 1960 Kennedy-Nixon debate reveal about television?
options: Visual appearance affects perception as much as substance on TV
